title: Layers into register
concept: An engineering drawing is presented as one sheet in a four-layer assembly. Drawing ink, stable port identities, unresolved calculations and human review first occupy separate spatial planes, then align without erasing their responsibilities. The proposed bypass visibly reroutes around Valve B and creates a second unresolved calculation and review path. All diagram content is illustrative; no engineering calculation or approval has been performed.
metaphor: Transparent engineering films on a registration bench: one coherent assembly, four independently traceable responsibilities.
choreography: A readable pump-and-valve drawing rises above three thin retained layers.
Four films separate vertically while shared port registration guides hold their identities in alignment.
The selected base route or proposed bypass is drawn above a detached calculation film; pressure loss remains explicitly unknown.
The original drawing recedes while an amber review film lifts forward with unresolved targets.
Drawing ink, port rings, calculation questions and review contours converge onto one registered proposal while the unapproved state stays visible.
interaction: The supplied Base route / Add bypass choice changes the path geometry in phase 2. Add bypass introduces a pink branch around Valve B, its branch valve, and a matching unresolved calculation trace; the chosen topology is retained through review and outcome.
contributions: Reusable isometric SVG film primitive with matching drawing, connectivity, calculation and review coordinate systems.
Registration choreography that reveals shared identities without flattening separate engineering responsibilities.
Choice-dependent bypass geometry, calculation uncertainty and review targets generated from a deterministic state.
limitations: All topology, equipment marks and overlays are illustrative and are not validated against a real P&ID or DesignGraph.
Pressure loss is shown as unknown; no hydraulic calculations, completeness checks or design approval are claimed.
The display omits detailed instrument identifiers and full port metadata to keep the illustration legible at small sizes.
No browser or device acceptance check was performed by this independent entry team.
